column2: Also on the authority of Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him): “Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Prophet ﷺ:
O Messenger of Allah, the people of wealth have gone off with the rewards: they pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give in charity from the surplus of their wealth.
He said: Has Allah not given you things with which to give charity?

Every tasbīḥah is a charity, every takbīrah is a charity, every taḥmīdah is a charity, enjoining good is a charity, forbidding evil is a charity, and in the intimate relations of one of you there is a charity. They said: O Messenger of Allah, does one of us fulfil his desire and have a reward for it?
He said: Do you not see that if he were to put it in something unlawful, he would bear a sin for it? Likewise, if he puts it in what is lawful, he has a reward.” Reported by Muslim.

Nāsan (“some”): they were the poor among the Emigrants, as the other narration makes clear. “Of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ”: aṣḥāb is the plural of ṣaḥb, one who met the Prophet ﷺ after his prophethood and before his death, believing in him, and died in that state.
Al-duthūr: plural of dathr, which is abundant wealth.
“From the surplus of their wealth”: from their wealth that exceeds their needs.
Buḍʿ aḥadikum (“the intimate relations of one of you”): it is used for intercourse and for the private part itself. Wizr: a sin.
The Companions' eagerness to race and compete in righteous deeds.
Charity is not restricted to wealth; rather, it may be better in other forms.
The virtue of saying subḥān Allāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, Allāhu akbar and al-ḥamdu lillāh, and of enjoining good and forbidding evil.
Bringing a righteous intention to mind in permissible matters, for they may then become acts of obedience.
Encouragement to marital relations because of the benefits in them: lowering the gaze, breaking desire so that it does not lead to the unlawful, and increasing offspring.

This hadith guides us to the fact that some of the poor among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, when they saw the wealthy Companions giving charity from the surplus of their wealth while also praying and fasting as they themselves prayed and fasted,

were saddened by their own inability to give charity and by the others' getting ahead. They complained to the Messenger ﷺ, and he told them that charity is not confined to wealth but is also in righteous deeds, including the remembrance of Allah—saying subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh and lā ilāha illā Allāh—enjoining good

and forbidding evil; and that in a man's relations with his wife there is a charity, because of the religious and worldly benefits in it, such as lowering the gaze, breaking desire so that it does not lead to looking [at what is unlawful] and to fornication, and producing offspring by which the world is populated and the nation made numerous on the Day of Resurrection, since the Messenger ﷺ urged that;

and the child benefits his parents in time of need in this world, and by supplicating and doing good deeds for them that benefit them in the Hereafter. And whoever gives charity from his wealth along with righteous deeds, that is from Allah's favour to him: “That is the favour of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great favour” [al-Jumuʿah 62:4].
On this meaning the poet said:
They feared Allah and none besides Him, so all feared them, / alike the inanimate things of creation and its beasts.
They girded themselves to attain every precious goal / and noble deed—too long to count—
until they reaped the fruit of love, after it had wronged them, / and love's torment became sweet.
The printed text reads صادقة, evidently for صدقة (“a charity”).
